title: IMSQRT squares components directly (flushing 1e-300 to "0"), treats #DIV/0! angles as 0, and leaves residue on -1
statement: In Excel 16.0 builds 20430 and 20527, IMSQRT(inumber) squares re and im directly (flushing subnormal squares < DBL_MIN to 0, and returning "0" if two finite squares sum to infinity), takes sum.sqrt().sqrt(), and uses IMARGUMENT(z)/2 with #DIV/0! angles mapped to 0, then multiplies by Excel's circular cos/sin. Consequently IMSQRT(1e-300) returns "0", IMSQRT(-1) returns "6.1257422745431E-17+i", and IMSQRT("1e-300-1e9i") returns purely real "31622.7766016838". All 2,029 full-bank IMSQRT rows match.
basis: Measured in CalcFunc-Evidence runs/w111-complex-kernels-20260929/answers/answers-imsqrt.json.gz and cache/w111-extended-regenerated-20260929/answers-imsqrt.json.gz (Excel 16.0 build 20430) plus Excel 16.0.20527.20088 (jnt_parity_complex row 422); 2,029/2,029 full-bank rows match.
